summary: Unbound agent-output derivation outbox + `derived_output` materialization-ledger path (cinatra#1893, Epic #1883 slice A5) — the operator-upgrade twin of the fresh-install bootstrap DDL in src/lib/drizzle-store.ts. Two additive changes backing the produces-scoped capture of an unbound WayFlow terminal-success run's final output: (1) `artifact_materializations_path_check` GAINS the value `derived_output` (the ledger path the post-terminal derivation job writes through the standard materializer) — a GUARDED CHECK widening that only re-asserts the constraint when it is absent or lacks the value, admits a new value, and rejects no pre-existing row (mirrors the core__0040 sa_assertedby_chk widening); (2) `agent_run_output_derivations` — the transactional outbox: ONE row per non-empty terminal-success run, inserted ATOMICALLY with the terminal status CAS + final-output snapshot (transitionRunStatus' derivationOutbox branch); PK run_id + ON CONFLICT (run_id) DO NOTHING makes capture idempotent under a stop/retry re-drive; `status` carries the derivation lifecycle (pending -> deriving [LEASED] -> done|no_match|no_produces) and a recoverable row lease serializes the one-shot job vs the reconciliation sweep. USER-LAND-AFFECTING (destructive:true) — it ALTERs the DEPLOYED artifact_materializations_path_check on an existing table (DROP+re-ADD CONSTRAINT), which the schema-migration ledger classifies destructive; but it is IDEMPOTENT, REVERSIBLE, and NON-DATA-DESTROYING (the widening only ADMITS a new value, rewrites/drops/rejects no existing row), plus one brand-new empty table (nothing REQUIRED, no data rewrite, no NOT NULL on an existing table). Rides node-pg-migrate's default single transaction; unqualified names resolve to the app schema on the runner's search_path. down() drops the outbox table and narrows the CHECK back only when no `derived_output` row exists (else leaves the harmless additive widening in place with a NOTICE). SEQ RENUMBERED to 0071 (merge-train ordering): core__0069 (assistant-thread-title-slug) shipped on origin/main and a sibling migration (cinatra#1986) merging ahead of this one in the train claims core__0070, so this migration takes the next genuinely-free sequence 0071 — strictly greater than the max shipped seq (rename-only, zero SQL diff). migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: owner approval required; the lane never merges.
